newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may have bought 300,000 tns U.S. soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may have bought 300,000 tns U.S. soybeans.

text.p: Recent talk in the Brazilian market that crushers have been buying U.S. soybeans may be linked to export sales to unknown destinations reported today by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, dealers said.

The latest USDA report included 331,600 tonnes sold to unknown destinations in the week to October 17 which led to speculation in Chicago that Brazil may have been a buyer of a substantial proportion of the total.
"The talk here is that crushers such as Ceval and Sadia have bought a total of five cargoes in recent weeks which would give around 300,000 tonnes," one trader said.
Officials at Sadia and Ceval were not immediately available to comment.
However no traders believed in another rumour that Brazil may also be buying soyproducts from the U.S.
"Brazil is buying soymeal and soyoil but from Argentina and Paraguay, not from the U.S.," one dealer said.
Brazilian traders have been talking since the beginning of this month about U.S. soybean purchases which they say have been done for drawback purposes and are not for the internal market.
Brazil is expected to import up around 1.3 million tonnes of soybeans in the 1996/97 marketing year (February/January), most of which will come from Paraguay and Argentina, dealers said.
-- Caroline Bullloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
